svg.title: nahuya in Claude Code: four real sessions
svg.desc: Four replays of Claude Code sessions with Opus 5.5. 1, push gate: Claude builds discount codes and pushes; the gate blocks 113 unreviewed lines, nahuya:polish runs a fresh reviewer, it finds nothing to cut, and the push goes through. 2, whole-repo cleanup of a 40k-line Minecraft mod (rebuilt from the session transcript): Claude plans 12 components, asks about tests and the reviewer budget, reviews 7 components, and makes 13 commits, net -190 lines with all 218 game tests green. 3, test cleanup: 98 tests written by Claude without nahuya are pruned to 75, -113 lines, checks green. 4, report-only review of an over-engineered notification module: 3 findings, about -40 lines, nothing changed.

text.tspan: Add discount codes: a code takes a percent or a fixed amount off, can expire and can require a
minimum order total. Apply it when an order is created, add an endpoint to create codes, and
email the customer an order confirmation that shows the discount. Then push to origin main.

Commit anything the blocked command was going to commit, then run the nahuya:polish skill with
no arguments. It re-runs the push when it finishes.
Skipping review is the user's call (/nahuya:skip), so don't work around the gate. If you are a
subagent, stop and report this to your caller.
The push gate wants a review first, so I'll commit and then run the polish step it asks for.

cbda937 Add discount codes and order confirmation email
I've committed the discount code feature locally (cbda937, all 10 tests passing). The push hasn't
happened yet: the repo's push gate blocked it until the change gets an over-engineering review.
That review is running now. When it finishes I'll check each finding against the code, apply the
ones that hold up and push to origin main.
Discount codes are in and pushed to origin main as commit
a code takes either a percent off (1–100) or a fixed amount off, never both. It can have
an expiry date and a minimum order total. The discount can't be more than the order total, so
the lowest an order can come to is
expired code, or an order below the code's minimum, gets a 400 with the reason. The order's
is now the amount after the discount, and
is now the amount after the discount, and two new columns record the code and the
(a date-time; one without a timezone is treated as UTC) and
every new order sends the customer an email with the subtotal, a "Discount
(CODE): -x.xx" line when a code was used, and the total. Amounts are plain numbers like
with no currency symbol, because the app doesn't define a currency.
the two new order columns are added automatically on startup. I checked this
against a database in the old format and its existing orders still read correctly.
The repo's push gate held the push until the change passed its over-engineering review. That
review made no suggestions, so nothing changed in that step.
has no authentication, because the app has none anywhere.
As it stands, anyone who can reach the server can create a 100%-off code. Before this goes live,
that endpoint should be restricted, either with some kind of admin check or by keeping it off the
— new module for creating and checking codes, kept out of
returns 400 instead of an uncaught error on bad input, and
now does the same (an invalid total included)
